title: 3. IOC vs TTP — Pyramid of Pain
objective: Study-guide review — ICCS423 v2 — L21: Threat Intelligence & MITRE ATT&CK: 3. IOC vs TTP — Pyramid of Pain.

blocks.text: This concept (David Bianco) is foundational. Master it.

items: Examples: IP, domain, URL, file hash (MD5/SHA-256), email address, registry key
Short shelf life — attackers rotate IPs, register new domains, repack malware (new hash)
Value: good for automated blocking, easy to bypass
Tactic — why (goal): Initial Access, Persistence, Exfiltration
Technique — how (method): Spearphishing Attachment, Scheduled Task, DNS C2
Procedure — specific implementation: "APT28 uses .xlsm macro → drops .exe in %APPDATA% → schedules task every 4 hours"
Long shelf life — changing TTPs requires retooling, retraining
Value: gold for detection engineering and threat hunting

blocks.text: `` ┌─────────────────┐ │ TTPs │ ← maximum pain to attacker ├─────────────────┤ │ Tools │ ├─────────────────┤ │ Network/Host │ │ Artifacts │ ├─────────────────┤ │ Domain Names │ ├─────────────────┤ │ IP Addresses │ ├─────────────────┤ │ Hash Values │ ← trivial pain, attacker re-packs └─────────────────┘ ``
Key insight: invest in TTP-based detection, not just IOC feeds. A new hash takes attackers 5 minutes; changing a TTP can take months.
